chapter: Life on the road and in the Webb band's book
title: The Selmer's carrying power at the Kansas City auditorium and Savoy
summary: McRae recalls not being heard in a crowd of 12,000 with the Conn and being heard clearly with the Selmer.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Big sound right around you. I remember when I played with Chick when we played in Kansas City -- what really got me against
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
the Conn horn, when we came back --

That's when I told you it was '37 when we was on the road. We played Kansas City that time. We saw Big Joe Turner and those people there. We went out to where Big Joe Turner and all those people were.
(Inaudible) Joe sing a song for an hour.
Like a whole half or forty-five minutes singing some blues up tempo.
We went up to hear him sing --
And we played the auditorium. It was such a big (inaudible). It had 12,000 -- 13 to 15,000 people in there.
And when I would get up to play a solo, and people standing -- (inaudible) guys from some music company hear me play, they was standing like five or six rows back.
And so many people there, they couldn't hear me. Unless I went to -- they say, 'Get into the mike, get into the mike.' You know, get into the mike.
But then when I came back and got the
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

Selmer, I played the Savoy -- the time I played against Benny, man, they could hear me all over the place. I was way on the end. I wasn't no where near a mike. The mike would be down in front, but there were no (inaudible). He told me to put a mike over there. I didn't need no mike. That horn would carry, you know. It had a lot of carrying power to it. You know, the mike would be up front. But if you didn't get right down into the mike, you know, you couldn't be heard. But I know when I stood up in the Savoy and played that horn, that horn would go out. Because a guy told me, "I could hear you way back in the back." It had good carrying power.
